title: The Cask of Amontillado
focus: revenge carried out with perfect control

teacherSummary.text: Montresor, vowing revenge for 'a thousand injuries' and an insult from Fortunato, lures the drunken wine connoisseur during carnival into his family catacombs with the promise of a rare cask of Amontillado. Deep in the vaults he chains Fortunato into a niche and walls him in alive. He tells the story fifty years later; no one has disturbed the bones.

context.history: The story (1846) is set during carnival in an unnamed Italian city. Its catacombs echo Roman and Parisian ossuaries. Amontillado is a Spanish sherry.

significance: It is a model of dramatic and verbal irony, from Fortunato's name ('fortunate') to the toast 'to your long life'. It is a Common Core Appendix B exemplar for grades 11–CCR.
discussionQuestions: Have you ever felt someone deserved to be paid back? What is the difference between justice and revenge?
